column7: The behavioural half of project-child-liveness-create-restore-001: two independent connection pools into one isolated schema, replica B running DeleteProject's full cascade between replica A's authorization and A's own child write. Four sites (#2702 CreateSecret, #2711 CreateFolder, #2710 CreateEnvironment, #2712 RestoreSecret); this row names the CreateSecret one, the other three are _CreateFolder_, _CreateEnvironment_ and _RestoreSecret_ in the same file. Each asserts the EFFECT -- the count of LIVE children under the deleted project -- not A's returned error, because A may legitimately fail OR be swept; what it may not do is leave a live child behind. The CreateSecret test additionally asserts no orphan version 1 survives, since the version is written in the same transaction. Each also asserts the interleaving actually happened (the one-shot hook fired) and that B's delete really committed, so a zero orphan count cannot be the vacuous consequence of the delete having failed. Red-proven by neutering the project re-check to answer "live" unconditionally -- the pre-fix behaviour, nothing else changed: all four go red with exactly one orphan child each, plus the orphan version. NOT covered, and stated in the file header rather than left to be assumed: the opposite interleaving where A's FOR SHARE lands first and the cascade blocks on it -- lockLiveParent's doc argues that order is safe, and the beforeA hook can only produce the order that caused the bug
